chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Our father informed us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn al-Nadhr, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

regarding a group of people who are on a journey, and one of them dies while the other is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), and they have with them a small amount of water sufficient for only one of them. Which one should they begin with? He (peace be upon him) said: The one in a state of major ritual impurity should perform the ritual bath (ghusl), and the dead body should be left [for later], because this [bath for the living] is an obligatory act (fard), and this [bath for the dead] is a tradition (sunnah).

key_terms.جُنُب: One in a state of major ritual impurity requiring full body washing

ai.seo_question: Which takes precedence in using limited water: the living person in major ritual impurity or the deceased?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy of ritual purity by prioritizing the living person's obligatory bath (ghusl al-fard) over the deceased's traditional bath (ghusl al-mayyit), which he classifies as a confirmed tradition (sunnah). This ruling, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between mandatory acts and recommended practices when resources are scarce, ensuring the living's immediate spiritual obligation is met first. The decision underscores the practical application of 'priority of the living' in ritual law, reflecting the Imams' focus on the dynamic needs of the community over static ceremonial forms.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 32-19 Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Nadhr that he had asked Abal Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.),

“Imagine that two people are on a journey. One of them passes away and the other one is in a state of major ritual impurity. There is only enough water for making the ablution of the corpse or the ablution of the person in a state of major ritual impurity. What should the water be used for?” Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) replied, “The person who is in a state of major ritual impurity should use the water for making ablutions, since this is an obligatory act. He should leave the dead, since making the ablutions for the dead is a part of the tradition (of the Prophet (S) and is not obligatory).”
